job.title: Finance Manager
job.description:
The Opportunity
You’ll lead the day-to-day delivery of Enatel’s accounts payable, accounts receivable and credit functions, with three direct reports and responsibility for setting priorities, maintaining service standards and resolving issues. The role sits at the centre of cash collection, supplier payments and working capital performance, so accuracy, pace and sound judgement all matter.

This is a hands-on finance leadership role with broader exposure across month-end, balance sheet control, budgeting, forecasting, cashflow, compliance and audit. You’ll coach the team, strengthen controls and improve the processes behind the numbers, while working closely with Finance, Sales, Procurement, Supply Chain and operational teams. Benefits include a flexible working policy, Southern Cross health insurance, LinkedIn Learning access, and a supportive team culture that invests in people’s development.

The Company
With operations across New Zealand and North America, Enatel is a growing hi-tech electronics company with a proven track record of success and innovation. More than 95% of everything it designs and manufactures on site is exported internationally, with intelligent software, efficient hardware and decades of power electronics design experience combining to deliver solutions that address industry needs.

Enatel's more than 200 talented employees support a valued customer base and highly successful product portfolio. The business invests in growth through its people and their development, with a culture that sees obstacles as opportunities and continuously improves. Part of the IDEAL Industries Inc. family, Enatel recently opened a purpose-built 8,000-square-metre facility at Dakota Park near Christchurch Airport.

The Role
Key responsibilities include:

  • Lead accounts payable, accounts receivable and credit management, setting priorities and ensuring accurate, timely processing, collections and stakeholder service.
  • Monitor ageing, overdue balances, payment activity and working capital measures, and coordinate prompt resolution of exceptions, escalations and control issues.
  • Support month-end close by reviewing reconciliations, journals and schedules, maintaining assigned balance sheet accounts and resolving anomalies.
  • Contribute to budgeting, forecasting and cashflow management through reliable inputs, supporting analysis and clear visibility of expected cash movements.
  • Maintain financial controls and audit-ready records, and support tax, statutory reporting and external audit requirements within agreed timeframes.
  • Improve AP, AR and related finance processes, strengthen ERP and data discipline, and maintain clear procedures for key controls and workflows.
  • Lead, coach and develop a team of three, creating clear expectations, accountability, collaboration and practical opportunities for capability growth.



Your Profile
You’ll bring:

  • A relevant tertiary qualification in accounting, finance or a related discipline. CA, CPA or an equivalent professional qualification is advantageous.
  • At least five years’ relevant commercial finance or accounting experience, including hands-on responsibility for core finance operations and leadership or supervision of a small team.
  • Strong practical knowledge of accounts payable, accounts receivable, credit management, month-end close, reconciliations and balance sheet control.
  • Experience supporting budgeting, forecasting and cashflow management, with strong Excel capability and practical experience using an ERP or integrated finance system.
  • Sound financial judgement, attention to detail and the ability to investigate issues, improve processes and communicate clearly across finance and non-finance teams. Experience in manufacturing, technology or another operational environment is advantageous.



How to Apply
Full working rights are required and no sponsorship is offered.

job.title: Payroll Administrator
job.description:
The Opportunity
You’ll be the person who makes sure Wyma employees in New Zealand and Australia are paid accurately and on time. Using the IMS payroll system, you’ll run the full payroll cycle — new starters, terminations, leave, allowances, reconciliations and statutory filings — while keeping everything compliant with local legislation.

You’ll also cross-train on MHM payroll so you can provide cover when the team needs it. That means you’ll build real dual-system knowledge and help create the operational resilience the business relies on.

This is a 12-month fixed-term role reporting to the Group Financial Controller. You’ll work closely with HR, Finance, managers and employees, and become a trusted point of contact for payroll questions. The environment values safety, teamwork, continuous improvement and integrity. The role is 30 hours per week.

The Company
MHM Automation designs and delivers automated systems for the food processing and logistics industries. Founded in Christchurch in 1884, the company has grown from a regional engineering business into a provider of processing, handling, chilling, freezing and packaging solutions for global food processors.

In 2024 MHM became part of Fortifi Food Processing Solutions, strengthening its presence across five continents. The group currently operates four business units — Wyma NZ, Wyma EU, Fabrication, and Materials Handling (recently merged with Chilling & Freezing).

People at MHM work with a safety-first mindset, treat each other as owners, focus on creating long-term customer value, continuously look for a better way, and do the right thing.

The Role
Key responsibilities include:

  • Process end-to-end payroll for Wyma employees on IMS for both New Zealand and Australian entities.
  • Ensure calculations for timesheets, leave, deductions, allowances, reimbursements and terminations are accurate and on time.
  • Maintain employee payroll data across IMS, Ostendo, Bamboo and Biotime, including starters, leavers and changes.
  • Reconcile payroll reports, investigate discrepancies and support month-end Finance requirements and audit requests.
  • Administer NZ (PAYE, KiwiSaver, ACC, Holidays Act) and Australian (PAYG, Superannuation Guarantee, awards) compliance obligations.
  • Respond professionally to employee and manager payroll enquiries and help people understand their payslips and leave.
  • Develop working knowledge of MHM payroll processes and provide cover during leave or peak periods; keep process documentation current.

Your Profile
You’ll bring:

  • Previous payroll administration experience, ideally with knowledge of New Zealand and/or Australian legislation.
  • Strong attention to detail, numerical accuracy and confidence using payroll and HR systems (IMS is an advantage).
  • Solid Excel skills and the ability to reconcile and investigate differences before payroll is finalised.
  • Clear communication and customer-service skills, with discretion when handling confidential information.
  • Organisational skills, the ability to meet deadlines independently, and a collaborative approach that fits a continuous-improvement culture.

Full working rights are required and no sponsorship is offered.

The team of commercial analysts are professional, self-sufficient and mostly made up of chartered accountants. You will lead them, resource them, and give them the strategic air cover so they can keep delivering the fact base the trading teams rely on. Your own time will go to the forward-looking work: annual trade budgeting, commercial governance, and the conversations that decide where the next sale, unit and dollar of profit comes from.

Foodstuffs South Island is the co-operative that feeds the South Island and works to create successful communities. It is one of the region’s largest employers, owned by its members and present in nearly every community across the island.
The Merchandise division sits at the centre of that. It negotiates with suppliers, manages the commercial terms that apply at product and supplier level, and partners with trading teams so the right product arrives for the right customer at the right cost. You will work alongside Retail, Supply Chain, Finance and the wider Merchandise leadership group.
The purpose is straightforward: better commercial outcomes that ultimately benefit members, customers and the communities the co-operative serves.

The Role
Your week will include:

  • Lead the commercial performance of the Merchandise function, identifying opportunities to maximise profitability, supplier value and member benefit.
  • Drive the annual trade budgeting process with Finance, Retail and the Heads of Business, then cascade and review it through the year.
  • Oversee supplier commercial agreements, trading terms and rebate programmes so activity matches expected commercial outcomes.
  • Partner with Merchandise, Retail, Supply Chain and Finance teams to surface, prioritise and deliver commercial opportunities.
  • Provide timely, accurate commercial insight that supports both operational decisions and longer-term strategy.
  • Lead and develop a high-performing commercial team, including performance, capability and succession.
  • Monitor commercial performance against budget and forecast, and lead the analysis and business cases that improve returns.

Your Profile
You will bring:

  • Significant leadership experience in a senior commercial, category, supplier management or business leadership role, typically 10–15+ years of relevant depth.
  • Proven ability to drive commercial performance and deliver financial outcomes in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment.
  • Strong commercial acumen, including experience managing supplier relationships, commercial negotiations and value-creation work.
  • The ability to influence senior stakeholders and contribute effectively as a member of a leadership team.
  • Experience developing and leading high-performing teams, preferably with analytical or accounting specialists.
  • Strong financial literacy and the capacity to move quickly from a high-level view to the detail that shows where money is made or lost.
  • Comfort operating in a high-performance culture: constructive challenge, clear expectations, and the temperament for pace and trade-offs.

Experience in FMCG, grocery retail, wholesale or distribution is an advantage, as is a CA qualification, but neither is a hard requirement. What matters is that you are commercially wired and forward-looking.
